assumptions.text: Expert routing is assumed perfectly balanced: every one of the 8 expert-parallel ranks receives exactly the mean token load. Real routing is skewed, and under synchronous EP the layer's wall clock is the busiest rank's, so the MoE step times and the all-to-all here are a lower bound rather than an estimate. Set `ep_load_factor` to the max/mean expert load from a routing trace to price it; the model carries no default for it, because a number nobody measured would read like one somebody did.

max_batch_total.description: TP/PP/EP share the same request set and CP splits one sequence across ranks — none of them run more requests. Only DP-attention and DP-replicas carry independent batches.
max_batch_total.label: Unique requests / cluster

max_prefill_batch.description: Prefill is activation-bound, not KV-bound, and does not coexist with decode: the KV pool is empty during the prefill forward, so its bytes are free for activations. Budget = the residual outside gpu_memory_fraction (activation + overhead) PLUS the whole KV pool decode would otherwise hold — i.e. the card minus weights and overhead. The per-stream footprint is the peak at B=1 and seq=min(input, prefill_chunk_size), so the ceiling plateaus once the prompt is longer than one chunk.
max_prefill_batch.label: Max prefill batch / DP rank
max_prefill_batch.symbolic: ((1 − gpu_memory_fraction) × mem_total − overhead_bytes + kv_pool_bytes) / peak_activation_bytes_per_rank(B=1, seq=min(input, chunk))

max_tokens_total.description: Only DP-attention and DP-replicas carry independent batches; TP/PP/CP/EP share the same token set across ranks.
max_tokens_total.label: Max unique tokens / cluster

gpu.notes: Rounded; NVLink 5 → 900 GB/s/dir; RDMA CX-7 → 50 GB/s/dir

kv_cache.shard_note: KV divided by 1× (CP only — no cached tensor carries a TP-divided axis)
